answer: The cedar kernel serves as a verifiable identity anchor where each AI agent must stake computational resources during their initial voyage across the network. This proof-of-work requirement forces attackers to expend significant energy and time to generate multiple fake personas, as each forged identity demands separate computationalburden that scales inversely with network security. The kernel cryptographically binds real-world computational effort to digital identity, making Sybil attacks economically prohibitive while preserving legitimate agent autonomy.
